Title: Director of Information Technology Services
Description:
**Description**
---------------

The City of Gaithersburg is seeking a visionary, collaborative, and service-oriented Director of Information Technology Services to join our dynamic senior leadership team. The IT Services Director oversees a talented and high functioning team of IT professionals who support the City's departments and their missions. The next IT leader will bring innovation and collaboration, working in support of City-wide goals to be a strategic partner in service delivery and smart IT solutions. This is a rare opportunity to serve in a pivotal role in a well-managed, effectively governed, incredibly diverse community with an exceptionally high quality of life.
  
  
As part of the Senior Leadership Team, the Director of Information Technology Services will have the opportunity to lead key City and departmental initiatives, drive operational excellence, and help shape the future of our City in partnership with dedicated department directors, elected officials, and community members. Applicants must have subject matter skills and knowledge, supervisory and management experience, and a track record in leadership working with a diverse workforce and affecting inclusive and effective outcomes. This position truly offers a skilled leader the opportunity to work in partnership with the City Manager and Senior Leadership Team to bring new perspectives, leadership, and additional innovation to further the City's mission, vision, core values, and long-range goals.
  
  
The IT Services Director reports directly to the City Manager. As a member of the City's senior leadership team, the Director collaborates with the City Manager, Assistant City Managers, and other department directors on strategy and policy to ensure that the City's mission, vision, core values, and long-range goals are incorporated into operational activities and services.

  

The position can accommodate both in-person and limited remote work at the discretion of the City Manager. Preparation for and attendance at meetings, events, and other work outside of regular business hours is required. Residency within the City of Gaithersburg is not required.
  
  
For more details about the role and the Gaithersburg community, please review the Position Profile [PDF].

**Job Functions**
-----------------

**The Position:**

The IT Services Director performs complex professional work in the planning, organizing, and coordinating of the development, implementation, and maintenance of the City’s electronic data processing, management information systems, and related operations. The Director provides leadership, direction, and advanced professional expertise and oversight to the Department and employees responsible for coordination of the IT services for the City and is responsible for short- and long-range planning of the City’s technical infrastructure to ensure that it supports current and future business needs.
  
  
The complete classification description for the Director of Information Technology Services position can be viewed here.

  

**The Department**:
  
The Information Technology Services Department consists of 16.67 FTE, including the Director. The department has four groups, IT Central Support Services, Business Systems and Transformation Services, Network Operations and Security Services, and GIS and Data Services. IT Central Support Services provides City staff with Tier I and Tier II technical support of hardware, software, and systems. Business Systems and Transformation Services is responsible for maintaining business systems throughout their full lifecycle – requirements, procurement, implementation, and ongoing maintenance. Network Operations and Security Services is responsible for network, server, and telecommunication infrastructure as well as physical and cybersecurity, including identity management, emails, files, firewalls, and desktop and server patching. GIS and Data Services is tasked with creating, implementing, and maintaining geographic information data standards and enterprise GIS systems.
  
  
The department has a budget of $3.3 million. In addition to its regular operational duties, some of the Department’s current projects include:

* Support of the new City Hall construction at 12 South Summit Avenue.
* Implementation of a Rubrik-based backup and disaster recovery system.
* Creation of comprehensive IT policies and procedures.
* Replacement of the City’s phone system.
* Implementation of resilient WAN connections at major facilities.
* Evaluation and implementation of Artificial Intelligence technologies.
* Implementation activities surrounding major Public Works GIS initiatives.
* Selection and implementation of a centralized data warehouse with analytical services and artificial intelligence capabilities.
* Selection and implementation of a Constituent Relationship Management system.
* Implementation of a new HRIS, Payroll and Time and Attendance system.
* Implementation of a comprehensive ITSM/ITAM system.
* Replacement of the meeting management system.
* Supporting the City’s upcoming 2027 elections.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business administration, computer science, information technology, cybersecurity, or related field.
* At least 10 years of experience managing information technology systems, the majority of which shall have been in a supervisory or managerial capacity.
* Valid driver's license.

**Desired/Preferred Qualifications:**

* Local government experience is desired; municipal government experience is strongly preferred.
* Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification; and/or
* Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)/Certified Information Security Manager (CISM); and/or
* Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Service Management (ITSM) certification; and/or
* Certified Geographic Information System Professional (GISP).

**The Successful Candidate:**  
The ideal candidate for the Director of Information Technology Services position is a proficient, accomplished and forward-thinking public sector leader who is passionate about transforming local government through technology and is dedicated to public service. This individual is a strategic thinker who can translate big-picture goals into actionable plans, while also possessing the hands-on practical expertise to ensure high-quality service delivery, technological security, and operational effectiveness. The ideal candidate demonstrates intellectual humility and curiosity, values the expertise and institutional knowledge of experienced staff, and fosters meaningful collaboration within the department and across the organization while building strong relationships with elected officials, community members, and regional partners. They will possess the ability to navigate sensitive issues and competing interests with diplomacy, fairness, and discretion.
  
  
An exceptional communicator and listener, the successful candidate understands the value of inclusive engagement, transparency, and trust-building. They are committed to cultivating a positive organizational culture, empowering and developing staff through coaching, recognizing collective accomplishments, and managing performance in a constructive, accountability-oriented manner. This person must be comfortable with ambiguity and change, capable of championing innovation while maintaining reliable IT operations, and skilled in balancing strategic priorities with available resources and long-term operational sustainability. With a solid understanding of information technology operations, public administration, municipal finance, and municipal operations, the ideal Director of Information Technology Services brings both a visionary mindset and an engaged leadership style. They are technically proficient and grounded in values of equity, integrity, and professionalism, and thrive in an evolving, team-oriented environment where collaboration, creativity, and service excellence are expected and rewarded.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

**Compensation**

The anticipated target hiring range is $175,00 to $200,000, depending on qualifications, with an excellent benefits package.

  
  

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates must complete and submit a brief online application and are required to attach the following supporting documents to the online application upon submission:

* Current Resume
* Letter of Interest
* List of References (at least 4 to include a manager [current/former], a subordinate, and a colleague). **Please note: References will not be contacted without permission from the applicant.**

Other supporting documents may be attached but are not required.  
  
  

**First review of applications will begin by December 11, 2026.** The position will remain open until filled; recruitment will close without notice when a sufficient number of qualified applications are identified or all hiring decisions have been made.

  

For more information about the position, contact the City Manager's Office at 301.258.6310 or cityhall@gaithersburgmd.gov. Questions regarding the online application process may be directed to the Department of Human Resources at 301.258.6327 or hr@gaithersburgmd.gov. For demographic and other information about the City of Gaithersburg, please click here.  
  
*Department Directors are in the unclassified service and not included within the City’s merit system. The successful candidate will be subject to a background investigation. Direct deposit of paychecks is a condition of employment for all City of Gaithersburg employees.*  
  
*The City has established an alcohol-free, drug-free, and smoke-free workplace which applies to any person employed by, conducting business with, or applying for a position with the City. Each employee, as a condition of their employment, may be required to participate in pre-employment and reasonable suspicion testing. Employees classified as safety sensitive are also subject to immediate post-accident and random testing.*

Title: Senior Program Manager
Description:
**About Citco**

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services, delivering end-to-end solutions and service to clients across its global organization.

**Role Purpose**

The Senior Program Manager is accountable for the strategic direction, integrated planning and end-to-end delivery performance of AXI within the Investor Relations Value Stream. In addition to the official Senior Program Manager title, the role fulfils the Value Stream Delivery Lead responsibilities for Investor Relations, ensuring that agreed outcomes and priorities are translated into a coherent roadmap, single governed backlog and measurable delivery plan.

As a member of the Investor Relations Value Stream Leadership Team, the role partners with the Value Lead, Technology Lead and Operations Lead to connect strategy with execution. The Senior Program Manager owns the overall flow and coordination of delivery, providing clear visibility of progress, capacity, cost, dependencies, risks, impediments and outcomes across AXI and related work.

As a Grade 4 leader, the Senior Program Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy and organizational influence. The role shapes delivery strategy, challenges constructively, resolves complex cross-functional constraints and represents the Value Stream in portfolio and executive forums. The position also includes formal line-management responsibility for staff within the Project Management Department, combining Value Stream delivery accountability with people leadership and capability development.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

Investor Relations Value Stream and AXI Delivery Leadership

* Fulfil the Delivery Lead role within the Investor Relations Value Stream Leadership Team, partnering with the Value Lead, Technology Lead and Operations Lead to turn agreed outcomes and priorities into executable delivery commitments.

* Own the integrated Investor Relations Value Stream roadmap, AXI program plan, single backlog and delivery performance, ensuring investment and execution remain aligned to agreed strategic objectives and measurable business outcomes.

* Lead a complex portfolio of projects and workstreams, balancing platform development, business change, operational readiness, releases and production priorities.

* Translate strategic direction and business cases into sequenced, achievable delivery plans with clear ownership, dependencies, milestones and success measures.
* Provide direction across cross-functional and globally distributed teams, creating alignment, pace, transparency, and accountability.
* Anticipate material delivery challenges and establish practical mitigation, recovery or escalation strategies before outcomes are affected.
* Act as the senior delivery authority for AXI and the Delivery Lead for the Investor Relations Value Stream, representing delivery in Value Stream, portfolio, executive and governance forums.
* Drive consistent delivery practices, delivery metrics and continuous improvement while allowing teams to apply fit-for-purpose Agile, Waterfall or hybrid methods.
* Coordinate cross-Value Stream demand and dependencies, negotiate sequencing with shared services and escalate priority decisions where demand exceeds available capacity.
* Manage Value Stream capacity, resource demand and allocation, ensuring commitments are realistic and delivery constraints are visible early.
* Lead quarterly planning, roadmap reviews, execution reviews and delivery governance across strategic change, client work, business requests, platform change and KTLO activity.
* Maintain one visible and prioritized backlog linking Value Stream outcomes and objectives to executable epics, stories and delivery commitments, with clear ownership and no orphaned work.
Establish and facilitate the regular Investor Relations Value Stream leadership cadence, ensuring shared ownership across value, delivery, technology and operations.  

**Value Stream Delivery, Flow and Ways of Working**

Integrated Planning, Governance and Financial Control

* Develop and maintain integrated Value Stream plans, roadmaps, budgets, forecasts, capacity and resource plans, and delivery scenarios across AXI and related Investor Relations outcomes.
* Establish proportionate governance across the full delivery lifecycle, including business case, scope, schedule, financials, quality, RAID, decisions, dependencies and benefits.
* Ensure program commitments are realistic and supported by sufficient capacity, funding, technical readiness and business ownership.
* Lead Value Stream prioritization and trade-off discussions where demand exceeds capacity or where scope, sequencing, cost, dependencies or risk require leadership or executive decision.
* Provide concise, evidence-based reporting on delivery confidence, financial position, outcomes and material constraints.
* Ensure program delivery complies with applicable Project Management Department, PMO, SDLC, risk and control requirements

**Technology Delivery and Release Oversight**

* Oversee delivery across the SDLC, ensuring requirements, design, engineering, testing, UAT, performance, release and production-readiness activities are integrated and governed.
* Partner with product, business and technology leadership to maintain alignment between business outcomes, platform priorities and technical execution.
* Coordinate cross-platform, cross-program and cross-Value Stream dependencies, ensuring demand, blockers and integration risks are visible, owned, sequenced and resolved.
* Ensure releases have clear acceptance criteria, quality evidence, operational readiness, communications, implementation and support arrangements.
* Own the health of the Value Stream delivery system, using flow, quality, capacity and financial data to identify bottlenecks, remove impediments, improve predictability and support continuous improvement.
Promote fit-for-purpose use of Agile, Waterfall and hybrid approaches rather than applying a single methodology by default.  

**Executive and Stakeholder Leadership**

* Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors, business leaders, technology leaders, operations, control functions and external partners.
* Communicate complex delivery matters clearly and directly, adapting detail and recommendations to the audience.
* Present program status, risks, dependencies, investment choices and strategic recommendations to senior governance forums.
* Create a consistent program narrative across stakeholders and ensure decisions, commitments and accountabilities are understood and followed through.
* Challenge constructively where delivery confidence, scope, sequencing, ownership or expected value is unclear.
* Navigate competing priorities and organizational complexity while protecting agreed program outcomes.

**People Leadership and Project Management Capability**

* Provide formal line management for assigned staff within the Project Management Department, including regular one-to-ones, objective setting, performance and development conversations, and support for career growth.
* Set clear expectations for delivery quality, professional conduct, stakeholder management, governance and accountability.
* Allocate and balance work across direct reports, considering program priorities, individual capability, development needs and sustainable workload.

Title: Director of Business Technology
Description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Keep Things Running**

* Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
* Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
* Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
* Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
* Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
* Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

**Own the Platforms**

* Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
* Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
* Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
* Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
* Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

**Govern and Teach**

* Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
* Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
* Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
* Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
* Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
* Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

**Team and Partners**

* Lead two on-site IT staff.
* Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
* Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

**WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR**

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

**Strong candidates will bring:**

* Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
* Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
* Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
* Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
* A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
* Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
* Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:

* An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
* A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
* A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
* The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
* Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

**REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

**LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT**

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This is a rare chance to shape how an established Canadian manufacturer builds and runs its technology at a moment when AI is changing who can create software.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

**TO APPLY**

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

*Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.*

Pay: $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Company events
* Disability insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Extended health care
* Life insurance
* On-site parking
* RRSP match
* Vision care

Application question(s):

* How many years of work experience do you have with IT Strategy?
* Have you built or significantly developed an IT, business technology, technology governance, or technology enablement function or process from the ground up?
* Do you have hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO, permissions, branch protection or repository governance?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 environments, including identity, MFA, endpoint management, and security?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering or supporting platforms such as Supabase, PostgreSQL, Netlify, Vercel, or similar technologies?

Experience:

* IT: 7 years (required)
* DevOps: 3 years (required)
* Microsoft Platform: 3 years (required)

Work Location: In person

Title: Head of Project - North Darfur, Sudan

Together with national and international partners, we respond to humanitarian crises and support long-term solutions that improve the living conditions for the most vulnerable people. We change and shape food systems, we are locally-led and globally connected. As an impact-oriented and human-centered organization, we use innovation, evidence and data-informed decision-making to continuously improve our work and contribute to #Zero Hunger.

Head of Project - North Darfur, Sudan\*

in Darfur

Medical/ Communications & Engagement

Education
---------

* University degree in communications, public relations, journalism, health sciences or related discipline
* Master’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, health sciences or related discipline required.

Knowledge
---------

* Eight (8) years’ professional experience in issues management, internal communications, public relations, public affairs/relations, social marketing, community consultation and media relations; experience in public health or a health care setting is preferred
* Five (5) years’ experience in leading people in a large, complex organization is preferred
* Demonstrated experience in managing relationships with elected officials at various levels (municipal, provincial and federal).

* In-depth knowledge of communications technologies and practices, social media, web and multi-media approaches.

* Professional accreditation in Public Relations or other communications-based professional organization is preferred

Responsibilities
----------------

Provides leadership and management direction to staff responsible for the external communications and engagement activities of the department. (30% of time)

* Establishes Public Health & Emergency Services’ brand and monitors resonance and reputation in the community
* Leads the development of Public Health & Emergency Services’ digital engagement and media relations strategies, conducting ongoing media relations activities for Public Health & Emergency Services, including preparing media products, organizing media conferences, and identifying and encouraging opportunities for positive media coverage
* Leads the development and implementation of Public Health & Emergency Services’ media relations program, which includes proactive and reactive engagement
* Works closely with municipal, provincial or federal communication counterparts to deliver joint announcements at media events or special events that involve or impact the Niagara Region
* Formulates and implements strategic communications plans to support Public Health & Emergency Services in building effective relationships with its external clients and stakeholders
* Monitors trends, issues and legislation that affect Public Health & Emergency Services or its stakeholders and recommends approaches or responses to address issues identified
* Researches, analyzes, plans, develops and implements communications plans and strategies designed to assist Public Health & Emergency Services in building positive relations with the public
* Advises the Medical Officer of Health, the Public Health Chief of Staff, the Chief of Emergency Medical Services, and the Senior Leadership Team on political and reputational risk management
* Contributes to Public Health & Emergency Services’ government advocacy efforts through liaising with the Strategic Communications and Public Affairs team
* Leads alignment of the department’s community outreach activities and provides department leadership to all health promotion activities
* Leads staff responsible for outreach and collaborations with primary care and the health care sector and physician recruitment

* Ensures alignment and coordination of activity and quality of output between teams under their direction
* Ensures focus is service excellence, communication/transparency, innovation, and data integrity and work flow integration.

* Ensures all people related issues, including recruitment, grievances and labour relations issues, are aligned to HR and Corporate standards and practices.
* Helps to break down barriers to employee success, ensuring collaboration and cooperation with other teams within their division and department
* Ensures Occupational Health & Safety policies, programs and practices are implemented, and maintained. This includes workplace inspections, monitoring, accident reporting and investigations, and ensuring any observed hazards or lapses in the functioning of OH&S processes, and other OH&S concerns are responded to promptly.
* Ensures all individuals under supervision have been informed of hazards and instructed on the necessary risk control and emergency response measures;

Leads internal communications in Public Health. Enables Public Health & Emergency Services leadership with building engagement, supporting culture and disseminating information across all levels of Public Health through communication strategies, creative services employee engagement expertise. (20% of time)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Leads the development and implementation of communication plans and strategies to support strategic business and operational activities and ensure consistency in key messages
* Leads the Public Health & Emergency Services employee engagement activities through the development and implementation of the department’s internal communications strategy, identifying engagement opportunities for staff at all levels.
* Ensures the implementation and evaluation of relevant elements of the Public Health & Emergency Services strategic plan
* Participates in Senior Leadership Team meetings, advising the Medical Officer of Health, Associate Medical Officers of Health, the Public Health Chief of Staff, Chief of Emergency Medical Services, and Directors on strategic business decisions, and confidential or sensitive issues
* Ensure all policies and standards related to communications, community outreach, and employee engagement are successfully incorporated, understood, and communicated
* Develops and prepares reports, briefs, and Regional Council committee reports as required
* Identifies and implements ongoing and issue-specific internal communications strategies for Public Health & Emergency Services to ensure that department and corporate strategic goals are being met.
* Anticipates potentially contentious issues that could face the Corporation or department and advises on best methods of proactively and positively addressing them
* Reviews and advises on major initiatives and measures undertaken within Public Health & Emergency Services
* Ensure ongoing communications and effective relationships with the Strategic Communications and Public Affairs team

Leads crisis and outbreak communications for Public Health & Emergency Services, identifying and monitoring potential risks to the Department and Corporation, and developing contingency plans to respond. (15% of time)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Member of Public Health & Emergency Services Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
* Backup communications member of the Niagara Region Emergency Operations Centre (REOC) unless the emergency is a health crisis or outbreak where Public Health is the lead for communications and information
* Provides leadership to anticipate and address potential controversial, politically-sensitive obstacles and/or conflicts that may impact Niagara’s success and reputation; assessing potential risks; developing strategies to address issues and remove barriers.
* Leads the development of the outbreak communications strategy, which includes risk communications, key message development, media relations, multi-modal digital engagement, internal communications, stakeholder relations and evaluation. Provides direction to Communications and Engagement staff, as well as other Public Health staff in the implementation of the strategy.
* During health-specific crisis or outbreak, provides counsel to the CAO, REOC, and Council
* During health-specific crisis or outbreak, directs local area municipality communication strategy and works in collaboration with communication counterparts.
* During health-specific crisis or outbreak, directs communications strategies for stakeholders including school boards and post-secondary institutions.

Financial Management (5% of time)
---------------------------------

* Develops, manages, and administers annual and multi-year Capital and Operating budgets for the operating unit ensuring support of Council’s objectives, financial transparency and accountability, monitoring budget adherence, identifying and explaining variances, and financial reporting is effectively managed in compliance with corporate financial policies
* Ensure goods and services are acquired in accordance with the procurement policy. Authorize the acquisition of goods and services for the operating unit and direct reports in accordance with the procurement policy and procedures

Special Requirements
--------------------

* An annual influenza vaccination is recommended.
* Regional staff strive to enable the strategic priorities of council and the organization through the completion of their work. Staff carry out their work by demonstrating the corporate values of service, honesty, choice, partnership and respect.

Title: Area Manager II, Canada Operations

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly workforce and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.  
  
Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.  
  
Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Area Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.
  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Support, mentor, and motivate your hourly workforce
* Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
* Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Quality Assurance, Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
* Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
* Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
* Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud
* Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
* Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

  
A day in the life  
As an Area Manager II at an Amazon fulfillment center, you'll act as a strategic leader overseeing upto 80 associates while driving department level operational improvements. You'll conduct planning sessions with your team, coaching them through operational challenges while developing their leadership capabilities. On a typical day, you'll partner cross-functionally with teams such as Quality, HR, and Safety to implement scalable process improvements that could impact 200+ associates across multiple workflows. You'll diagnose root causes of performance gaps using advanced analytics, facilitate alignment meetings with senior leadership on department-level goals, and make data-driven decisions that balance competing priorities. You would leverage your strategic thinking to review department-wide metrics, and plan initiatives that directly impact millions of customer orders while maintaining high levels of engagement, safety, quality, and productivity standards.

* 2+ years of employee and performance management experience

* Experience in the management of large teams (50+ members)

* Experience in one or more of the following industries: shipping/logistics distribution centers, manufacturing environments, hospitality, healthcare, retail, and customer-facing / customer-service environments

You are accountable for your team's performance and for demonstrating how Delivery Management support improves delivery. You work with Product, Engineering, and internal partners to agree on meaningful measures of success, establish a starting point, and use results to guide action.

Delivery Management works as part of the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org, which brings together delivery support, engineering practices, workflow capabilities, investment and capacity information, and performance insights. You involve the right leaders when a solution crosses functional or team boundaries.

Delivery Manager support may focus on a product area, a problem spanning several products or product groups, a mission team, or a High Integrity Commitment. You recognize where support will help and when it should change or end. Product Managers retain product and business responsibilities, Tech Leads retain technical decisions and delivery accountability, and product teams retain their commitments. Delivery Managers help reduce process and tooling inefficiencies that prevent teams from delivering effectively.

For example, a Delivery Manager identifies recurring delays. You bring together the appropriate leaders in the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org to examine the data and address the causes, which may involve automation or a new capability. The team and Delivery Manager assess whether delivery improves. You ensure actions have owners and unresolved issues reach the accountable leaders who can address them.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Build and lead the team.** Lead recruiting, onboarding, coaching, and performance management. Set expectations for each Delivery Manager level, give regular feedback, and build development and succession plans. Encourage peer learning and share approaches that work, adapting practices to the problem. Recommend hiring, promotion, termination, and staffing decisions for supervisor review and approval.

**Set direction for your team.** Translate department priorities into team goals and work plans. Agree objectives with your supervisor and plan staffing, assignments, and development needs over the next 6-12 months. Review progress and adjust plans as needs change.

**Provide support where it adds value.** Work with Product and Engineering leaders to understand support needs. Match assignments to each Delivery Manager's experience, skills, and available capacity. Resolve competing requests within agreed priorities and staffing. Bring decisions about additional capacity or changes in direction to your supervisor.

**Make responsibilities clear.** Agree on the problems to address, support needed, expected results, and delivery success metrics with Product and Technology leaders and internal customers. Review results with those partners, your team, and your supervisor to determine whether more help is needed or support should move elsewhere, be reduced, or end. Coach Delivery Managers to spot problems early while leaving routine coordination with the teams and leads closest to the work.

**Own your team's results.** Set clear performance expectations for Delivery Managers and assess their effectiveness using agreed metrics and outcomes, supported by data and feedback from internal customers and Product and Engineering leaders. Challenge updates that describe activity without showing progress. Address signs that delivery support is becoming ongoing ownership of team ceremonies, routine project coordination, or project management office oversight. When work stalls, understand why, address the issue, and make sure the next action and owner are clear.

**Resolve issues that need leadership.** Help Delivery Managers address problems beyond their authority or experience. Bring the right decision-makers together and follow through on agreed actions. Handle day-to-day team decisions independently. Seek guidance on complex assignments, competing department priorities, or decisions beyond your authority; obtain supervisor approval for strategic decisions affecting team objectives.

**Turn recurring problems into shared improvements.** Use data and feedback to identify repeated delays and unnecessary effort. Challenge practices that are not helping and bring recommendations to leaders who own or are affected by the issue. Establish a starting point, then agree on improvement actions, owners, expected results, and timing. Follow through to determine whether changes helped, adjust when needed, and raise unresolved issues.

**Work as one organization.** Regularly speak with Product and Engineering leaders and your peers in the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org. Understand where teams are succeeding and where support could help. Hold Delivery Managers accountable for sharing findings and opportunities and involving the appropriate leaders in solutions. Each functional leader retains ownership of their team's capabilities and tools.

**Coordinate Delivery Manager and Program Management support.** Work with Program Management leadership when assignments need sustained technical planning and coordination, including operational work or work outside the Product Operating Model. Make responsibilities clear when someone serves in a Delivery Manager or Program Management capacity, and when that assignment changes.

**Make delivery information reliable and useful.** Hold Delivery Managers accountable for working with teams and information owners to keep needed information accurate, current, and available in agreed tools such as Jira. Use existing information before asking for separate updates. Work with system owners and affected leaders when information is missing or hard to capture, find, or interpret. Partner with the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org to establish consistent definitions, reliable data sources, and practical reporting for the agreed key performance indicators (KPIs). Ensure results are shared and reviewed with internal customers and appropriate leaders to guide decisions and improvement actions.

**Contribute to staffing and budget plans.** Contribute staffing and development needs to budget planning with the appropriate leaders in the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org. Manage assignments within approved staffing and funding, and apply company policies consistently.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Employment Experience***

  

* At least 7 years of experience in delivery management, program management, or related software delivery roles, plus at least 2 years of staff-management experience.
* Experience hiring, coaching, reviewing performance, and developing delivery professionals supporting multiple product teams or product areas.
* Experience working with empowered product teams and understanding how Product Operating Model delivery support differs from operational or other program management.

***Technical Skills***

**Technical Acumen**

* Strong understanding of software delivery from discovery through development, release, and production support. Able to coach Delivery Managers and have useful conversations with engineering leaders. No coding required.
* Working knowledge of iterative and continuous delivery, technical dependencies, release readiness, and program coordination. Able to choose an approach that fits the work.
* Proficiency in Jira and Confluence. Able to explain information, workflow, and automation needs to tool owners and use delivery information to support decisions.

**AI & Agentic Delivery Practices**

* Effective use of everyday AI tools such as Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT for research, communication, analysis, and delivery work. Able to coach the team on responsible use.
* Understanding of AI-enabled and agentic delivery practices. Able to spot useful automation opportunities, assess whether they help, and support the team in learning new tools and practices.
* Working knowledge of AI-DLC practices and guardrails. Able to identify adoption problems and work with Engineering and the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org on improvements.

**Delivery Rigor, Lean Process & Flow Metrics**

* Experience setting team goals and work plans, balancing support demand and capacity, and matching assignments to people's skills.
* Experience using root-cause analysis, continuous improvement, and flow measures such as cycle time, throughput, work in progress, and aging work to understand problems and assess improvements.
* Able to agree on meaningful KPIs with internal customers, partners, and the broader Technology Delivery and Engineering Enablement org to assess Delivery Manager effectiveness and demonstrate measurable delivery improvements.

***Additional Skills & Competencies***

* You've managed and developed delivery professionals. You can explain how your hiring, coaching, and performance decisions helped people work more effectively and independently.
* You take ownership. You raise concerns early, bring practical recommendations, and follow through. You are comfortable challenging an approach, having a difficult conversation, and holding people accountable for agreed actions.
* You understand empowered product teams and know when support will help and when it would take ownership away from their leaders.
* You make sound decisions when there is no established solution. You investigate the problem, use data and evidence to test your understanding, weigh the options, and know when to seek guidance or approval.
* You can balance competing support needs, explain your decisions, and change course when the situation changes.
* You build relationships with other leaders, recognize what is working, and turn shared problems and opportunities into action. You develop your team's judgment rather than becoming the person who solves every difficult problem.

**Collaboration & Communication**

* Strong people-management skills, including feedback, performance management, career development, succession planning, and coaching experienced individual contributors.
* Able to explain risks and choices clearly, challenge an approach respectfully, and work with senior leaders to resolve issues.
* Experience working across functions to agree responsibilities, address information gaps, coordinate action, and check whether improvements helped.

**Education Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in business, technology, or a related field, or equivalent education and/or work experience. Relevant certifications or continued learning in agile leadership, Kanban, continuous improvement, or program management are a plus.

**This Isn't the Right Fit If…**

If you focus on staffing and assignments without taking ownership of your team's performance, developing your people, building relationships with leaders, and turning delivery problems and opportunities into action, this role will not be a good fit.

If your first response to a delay is another approval step, mandatory meeting, or status report, you'll struggle here. You need to understand what is causing the problem and help address it without introducing unnecessary oversight.

If you prefer to solve every difficult problem yourself, this role will require a shift. You are responsible for developing Delivery Managers who can make sound decisions and follow through independently.

If you are comfortable identifying problems but leaving the next steps to someone else, this role will not be a good fit. You are expected to recommend action, agree responsibilities, and follow through on your team's commitments.

**In Your Application, Tell Us About…**

**A delivery team you built or developed.** How did you hire, coach, and manage performance? What could people handle independently afterward?

**A time support demand exceeded your team's capacity.** How did you choose where to assign people, explain the tradeoffs, and adjust the plan?

**A problem you noticed and took action to resolve.** What evidence did you use, what did you recommend, and how did you know the change helped?

**An improvement that required several teams to work together.** How did you agree owners, keep commitments moving, and handle missed actions while respecting each leader's responsibilities?

**A successful approach you helped others build on.** What was working, how did you help others use it, and what improved?

**The Senior Manager of Delivery Management is valued for building capable teams, taking ownership of their team's results, and working with partners to improve delivery. Compensation reflects the people-management responsibilities and scope of the role.**

**Job Summary**
The
**Operations Manager, Vendor Relations**
will be responsible for the strategic oversight, operational governance, and day-to-day contract management of RadNet’s third-party Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) partnerships. This includes managing Statement of Work (SOW) compliance, operational performance, and quality delivery across nearshore and offshore contact center partners, specifically scheduling operations and offshore administrative and back-office operations.
  
  
This role serves as the primary operational liaison holding vendor leadership accountable to strict Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), headcount adherence, and billing reconciliation. The Operations Manager will organize, lead, and drive all vendor governance meeting cadences (weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews), manage Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs), and partner cross-functionally with Workforce Management (WFM), Quality Assurance (QA), IT/Telephony, and Regional Operations to ensure seamless patient experience and cost-efficient operational delivery.
  
  
**You Will**

* SOW & Contract Governance: Manage and enforce all operational terms, deliverables, obligations, and performance benchmarks defined within vendor Statements of Work (SOWs) and Master Services Agreements (MSAs) across all outsourced partners.
* Vendor Accountability & Performance Management: Hold vendor operational leadership strictly accountable for contractual KPIs including Inbound Average Handling Time (IAHT), Call Quality/QA scores, Idle Time, occupancy, adherence, Abandonment Rates, Average Schedule Rate, and Monthly Attrition thresholds (monthly).
* Offshore Administrative Operations Management: Oversee and manage the daily operational workflows, accuracy, turnaround times, and productivity of offshore back-office administrative teams supporting order entry, document administration, medical records requests, insurance validation support, and pre-service tasks.
* Governance Meeting Cadence Leadership: Organize, lead, and establish structured agendas for all recurring vendor governance sessions, including:

+ Weekly Operational & Performance/QC Reviews: Tactical review of SLAs, error trends, and immediate corrective action plans.
+ Weekly Quality Control Calibration: Joint calibration between RadNet and vendor quality teams to ensure consistent evaluation and scoring standards.
+ Weekly Workforce Management (WFM) & Staffing Reviews: Analysis of roster headcount adherence, schedule lock-in, intraday forecasting, and shrinkage mitigation.
+ Weekly Regional Operations Touchpoints: Alignment between regional contact center leaders and dedicated vendor pods.
+ Monthly KPI & Invoice Reconciliation: Audit of monthly billed hours against actual telephony dispositions, validation of penalty deductions, under-staffing fee reductions, and contractual service level credits.
+ Monthly Dedicated Training Reviews: Curriculum alignment, evaluation of nesting graduation rates, and planning for new skill/protocol rollouts.
+ Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR): High-level strategic review with executive leadership evaluating operational trends, capacity expansion, technology integration, and overall partnership health.

* Financial & Billing Auditing: Rigorously validate monthly vendor invoices against telephony data (Five9/telephony reports) and approved billable dispositions (Available, Production, Approved Meetings, Approved Nesting/Upskilling). Enforce under-staffing penalty credits, non-billable overages, and downtime limitations for platform outages or local vendor issues.
* Remediation & PIP Management: Identify operational bottlenecks, performance dips, or quality variances; mandate, evaluate, and monitor vendor-submitted Corrective Action Plans and formal Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs) to swift resolution.
* Technology & Workflow Integration: Collaborate with internal IT, Telephony, and PMO teams to support vendor access, provisioning, and workflow execution across core RadNet platforms, including Five9 telephony, Salesforce P360, eRAD RIS, and secure enterprise workspaces.
* Training, Onboarding & Nesting Oversight: Partner with internal training teams to ensure vendor new-hire onboarding, 20-day "Ready State" certifications, attrition replacement training (at vendor expense), and compliance training are executed to RadNet standards prior to live production.
* Offshore Compliance & Data Security: Enforce strict adherence to HIPAA, protected health information (PHI) safeguards, ISO/HITRUST security standards, and offshore resource utilization policies in coordination with RadNet Information Security and Compliance.

**If You Are**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Operations Management, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Demonstrated experience managing offshore/nearshore vendor operations, including contact center scheduling teams and offshore administrative/back-office transaction processing.
* Proven track record of managing, enforcing, and interpreting vendor contracts, Statements of Work (SOWs), SLA credit models, and invoice reconciliations.
* Understanding of contact center metrics, WFM scheduling principles (e.g., Calabrio, IEX, Verint), telephony platforms (e.g., Five9, Cisco), and CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce).
* Exceptional leadership and facilitation skills with demonstrated ability to chair executive governance reviews, run multi-stakeholder operational meetings, and enforce accountability.
* Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills; advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, modeling, variance analysis) and reporting dashboards.
* Strong written, verbal, and cross-cultural communication skills, with experience managing cross-border distributed teams across multiple time zones.
* Must be able to maintain strict confidentiality of patient (HIPAA/PHI) and enterprise proprietary data.

**Preferred**

* Formal project management or process improvement certification (PMP, Six Sigma Green/Black Belt) is an asset.

Title: Program Controls Advisory Services Manager
Description:
When you care deeply about the work you do, it’s rewarding to see it through from concept to completion. We partner with clients to provide both program management and construction management to strategize, plan, and implement projects that drive organizations forward. From hospitals and airports to university campuses, mass transit systems, water treatment facilities, mines, and wind farms, we've successfully managed thousands of projects.

Joining our team, turning visionary ideas into reality, will shape your future—and the future of your community.

We are strategizing, planning, and implementing projects that help clients achieve their organization’s objectives. Join our award-winning program management team and bring transformational project solutions to life.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking qualified candidates for a Program Controls Advisory Services Manager position. The individual serves as a senior advisor to major capital programs, providing strategic Program Controls leadership during program mobilization, execution, transformation and periods of performance challenge.

The role operates at the intersection of client needs, Program Management and Program Controls, translating client objectives into practical governance, processes, systems, reporting and decision-making frameworks. Unlike a traditional Program Controls Manager focused on day-to-day delivery for one program, this role is deployed where specialized leadership, independent perspective or intervention is required.

The position establishes new controls organizations, assesses and strengthens existing programs, resolves complex delivery issues, improves underperforming controls environments and supports program leadership in restoring confidence, integration and predictability. It also acts as a trusted bridge among the client, PMO, delivery partners, consultants, contractors and internal controls teams.

This position requires prior experience working on an integrated program team with strong knowledge and hands-on experience in developing baseline project budgets and schedules; monitoring and tracking the progress of project work relative to established budgets and schedules; preparation of project budget and schedule status reports and presentations; working with Program/Project Managers to proactively identify project budget and schedule problems and implement corrective actions; and preparation of cost accruals, estimates to complete and estimates at completion.

Qualified candidates understand the process of administering the non-technical elements of large projects that are tied together for the successful delivery of a program. They are comfortable developing and maintaining procedures that help streamline project controls processes and provide mentorship to other project controls specialists and team members. They possess emotional intelligence and prioritize establishing and maintaining trusting relationships and close partnerships with Program/Project Managers, other team members and supporting them in serving the client and meeting established goals to achieve success

Your Key Responsibilities

Program Mobilization and Setup

* Advise clients and program leadership on fit-for-purpose Program Controls operating models for major capital programs.
* Develop governance frameworks for cost, schedule, risk, change, forecasting, funding, performance measurement and reporting.
* Establish integrated WBS, CBS, OBS, control accounts, coding structures, baselines, calendars, reporting cycles, roles, responsibilities and approval authorities.
* Develop Program Controls Plans, procedures, SOPs, workflows, responsibility matrices and reporting standards.
* Evaluate and recommend PMIS, scheduling, cost, risk and business-intelligence solutions, including Primavera P6, Primavera Unifier, e-Builder, Power BI and enterprise ERP platforms.
* Create scalable controls that mature across planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning and closeout.

Program Controls Advisory

* Serve as a senior advisor to Program Directors, Program Managers, PMO leaders and client executives on program performance and controls strategy.
* Independently assess whether controls are producing reliable information that management can use with confidence.
* Translate complex controls data into executive-level insight on current status, forecast direction, changes, risks and required decisions.
* Challenge ineffective practices and recommend practical improvements aligned with program maturity, complexity, risk profile, contracting strategy and delivery model.

Program Intervention and Issue Resolution

* Rapidly assess controls maturity and identify root causes of performance issues.
* Evaluate schedule quality, cost performance, forecast reliability, risk exposure, change governance, funding alignment and reporting effectiveness.
* Identify breakdowns among cost, schedule, risk, change, funding, contracts and program decision-making.
* Develop and lead targeted recovery and corrective-action plans with clear owners, milestones and performance indicators.
* Resolve unclear ownership, inconsistent processes, disconnected data, reporting gaps and ineffective functional interfaces.
* Stabilize underperforming controls environments and remain engaged long enough to embed sustainable improvements.

Client Services and Client Advocacy

* Serve as a trusted advisor between the client and the program delivery organization.
* Understand client objectives, funding constraints, governance requirements, risk tolerance and performance expectations.
* Translate client needs into clear, actionable requirements for the PMO and delivery teams.
* Facilitate difficult conversations involving performance, forecast changes, schedule delays, risk exposure, funding constraints and delivery challenges.
* Provide an objective perspective where client expectations and delivery realities are not aligned.
* Build trust through transparent, data-driven advice while maintaining productive stakeholder relationships.

Program Performance and Integration

Promote an integrated management environment in which Scope -> Schedule -> Cost -> Funding -> Risk -> Change -> Forecast -> Decision operate as a connected system.

* Ensure cost forecasts reflect schedule progression, approved changes and known risks.
* Ensure schedule forecasts consider procurement, funding, contractor capacity and delivery constraints.
* Connect quantified risk exposure with contingency and management reserve strategies.
* Improve consistency between project-level and program-level reporting.
* Develop forward-looking indicators that identify emerging issues before they become significant performance problems.

Governance and Program Assurance

* Conduct health checks and maturity assessments of Program Controls organizations.
* Assess compliance with procedures and governance expectations, including gaps between documented and actual practices.
* Establish escalation thresholds, decision rights and approval authorities.
* Support executive governance forums with concise, decision-oriented performance information.
* Review data quality and reporting reliability before information is elevated to client executives.
* Support independent program reviews, recovery initiatives and performance-improvement efforts.

Leadership and Capability Building

* Mentor Program Controls Managers and professionals across cost, schedule, risk, change, forecasting and reporting disciplines.
* Coach program leadership on using controls information for timely decisions.
* Establish clear interfaces among PMO leadership, controls functions, delivery teams and clients.
* Build collaborative multidisciplinary teams and reduce functional silos.
* Develop repeatable standards, frameworks, templates and leading practices for deployment across programs.
* Plan knowledge transfer so improvements remain with the program after the advisory engagement ends.

Typical Engagements

* A new multi-year capital program needs its controls organization established.
* A PMO is being formed, reorganized or transitioned.
* A client needs an independent assessment of Program Controls.
* Forecasts or schedules are not credible, consistent or decision-ready.
* Projects report differently, preventing program-level visibility.
* Risk, contingency, funding and change are disconnected from cost and schedule.
* Leadership does not trust dashboards or performance reporting.
* Systems are fragmented, overly complex or underutilized.
* Client and Program Management expectations have become misaligned.
* A program requires stabilization, turnaround, recovery or knowledge transfer.

The successful candidate should:

* Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Have the demonstrated ability to encourage and facilitate collaboration and cooperation amongst diverse team members
* Schedule and lead coordination meetings
* Work in a manner to ensure personal safety and that of fellow employees by following company health and safety guidelines and policies.
* Consistently adhere to Company processes and policies including business conduct, cyber-security, safety and personal conduct.

It is expected the successful candidate will have the following qualifications:

* Combination of a degree from an accredited institution in an applicable field or documented experience specific to program controls
* BA/BS Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Finance, Project Management or a related discipline.
* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is preferred
* Additional certifications, PgMP, PMI-SP, PMI-RMP, PMI-CP, CPA, CCM, PE, FE, or similar certifications is preferred
* A minimum of 15 years’ progressive experience supporting complex capital programs, including substantial Program/Project Controls leadership experience infrastructure/buildings/utility/water programs is required
* Familiarity with various project delivery methods, including Design Bid Build, Progressive Design Build, CMAR, and Design Build.
* Demonstrated success establishing, transforming or leading Program Controls functions on major infrastructure or capital programs.
* Strong knowledge of cost management, forecasting, scheduling, risk and opportunity management, change management, funding and cash-flow planning, performance reporting, PMIS/ERP environments and program assurance.
* Experience in the municipal sector in areas of public works, utilities, transportation, and industry and on multi-sector programs is preferred
* Experience in owner, PMCM, consultant, contractor or integrated delivery environments and advising senior client leadership.
* Must be able to demonstrate good interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
* Must demonstrate organizational skills and ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.
